contributions.statement: Generate acceptance/unit-test oracles from the specification in a context that cannot see the implementation or the coding agent's conversation, and do not let the same model write the tests right after writing the code: exposing the generated (faulty) code to the test generator cut fault detection by ~8-18 points per model (5/5 models, 3 Python benchmarks, Mann-Whitney p<0.05), and adding the spec alongside the code did not recover it (prompt+code was no better than code-only).
contributions.evidence: §VI-A Fig.2/Table II (prompt-only vs prompt+code significant for all 5 models, mean -13.2 pts; prompt+code ~= code-only); §VI-C Fig.4/Table IV (test-driven vs same-session agentic +7.9-17.7 pts, all significant). Caveats: Python function-level tasks; faults are LLM-generated and the hardest-per-task is selected; per-arm sample size unreported; paired design analyzed with an unpaired test; absolute 14%/25% appear only in the abstract.

contributions.statement: Do not tune or gate agent test-generation on test count or statement coverage as a proxy for fault detection: here spec-derived tests often reached the buggy line less often (lower fault-triggering) yet detected more faults, and CoVe/CoT produced up to ~2x more tests and similar coverage without detecting more, so the lever is oracle/assertion correctness, not volume or coverage.
contributions.evidence: §VII-A Tables V-VI and Fig.5: no consistent coverage-vs-detection relationship; higher test count (CoVe) did not raise detection; fault-triggering and fault-detection not consistently correlated. Oracle correctness is inferred, not directly measured (the authors concede this), so the mechanism is weakly supported.

reason: One contribution qualifies and is directly on point for the team's SDD rollout: keep the test/acceptance oracle independent of the implementation (feed it the spec, not the code or the coding agent's chat), a robust directional effect across 5 models and 3 benchmarks that refines the same-model-co-evolution finding in 2608.16742/2610.02952. The coverage/count nuance stays weak because oracle correctness is inferred rather than measured, and the headline absolute rates are abstract-only.
